reason: The text features several non-royal characters who exercise significant agency: Shaphan the scribe actively receives the Book of the Law, reports findings to the king, and reads the text aloud; Hilkiah the high priest finds and delivers the book; Huldah the prophetess receives a delegation and delivers God's word with authority; and other officials like Ahikam, Akbor, and Asaiah are sent on a mission. Additionally, 'the people of the land' (עַם־ הָאָרֶץ) exercise collective agency in anointing and making Jehoahaz king. These are bureaucratic officials, religious functionaries, and common people (not royalty) who take actions and make decisions that advance the narrative.
